string-array.name: descriptionYogaWarrior1Pose
string-array.item: Warrior 1 Pose
The Warrior 1 Pose (Virabhadrasana I) is a foundational yoga posture that strengthens the legs, opens the hips, and improves balance while stretching the chest and shoulders.
This pose engages the lower body while promoting flexibility in the upper body, making it a great full-body stretch.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a standing position (Tadasana) with your feet hip-width apart.
2. Step one foot back, keeping the toes slightly turned outward and the front knee bent at a 90-degree angle.
3. Extend both arms overhead, palms facing each other.
4. Keep your torso upright, engaging your core and pressing evenly through both feet.
5. Hold for a few breaths, then switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your front knee aligned over the ankle to prevent strain.
2. Engage your core to support balance and avoid arching your lower back.
3. Relax your shoulders and keep your gaze forward or slightly upward.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaWarrior2Pose
string-array.item: Warrior 2 Pose
The Warrior 2 Pose (Virabhadrasana II) strengthens the legs, improves flexibility in the hips, and enhances endurance.
This posture encourages body awareness and mental focus while promoting stability and alignment.
To perform the exercise:
1. Begin in a standing position and step one foot back, turning it perpendicular to the front foot.
2. Bend the front knee at a 90-degree angle while keeping the back leg straight.
3. Extend both arms out parallel to the floor, palms facing down.
4. Keep your torso upright and gaze over the front hand.
5. Hold for a few breaths before switching sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your front knee aligned with the ankle and avoid collapsing inward.
2. Press evenly through both feet to maintain stability.
3. Engage your core and lengthen the spine for proper alignment.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaWarrior3Pose
string-array.item: Warrior 3 Pose
The Warrior 3 Pose (Virabhadrasana III) is a balancing pose that strengthens the legs, core, and back while improving concentration and posture.
This pose challenges stability and coordination while providing a deep hamstring stretch.
To perform the exercise:
1. Begin in a standing position with feet hip-width apart.
2. Shift your weight onto one leg while extending the opposite leg straight back.
3. Hinge forward at the hips, bringing your torso parallel to the floor.
4. Extend both arms forward or keep them at your sides for balance.
5. Hold for a few breaths, then switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core to support balance and prevent wobbling.
2. Keep the lifted leg in line with the torso and hips square.
3. Maintain a soft bend in the standing knee to avoid hyperextension.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaHumbleWarriorPose
string-array.item: Humble Warrior Pose
The Humble Warrior Pose (Baddha Virabhadrasana) is a deep forward-bending variation of Warrior 1 that opens the chest, shoulders, and hips.
This pose enhances flexibility in the legs and spine while promoting grounding and inner focus.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in Warrior 1 Pose with arms extended overhead.
2. Interlace your fingers behind your back and straighten your arms.
3. Hinge forward at the hips, bringing your torso inside the front leg.
4. Allow your head to relax downward while lifting your interlaced hands overhead.
5. Hold for a few breaths before switching sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your front knee stable and aligned over the ankle.
2. Focus on deep breathing to enhance the stretch and maintain stability.
3. Relax your shoulders and avoid tensing the neck.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaReverseWarriorPose
string-array.item: Reverse Warrior Pose
The Reverse Warrior Pose (Viparita Virabhadrasana) is a graceful side stretch that strengthens the legs and opens the ribcage.
This pose promotes spinal flexibility while enhancing balance and stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Begin in Warrior 2 Pose with your front knee bent.
2. Lift your front arm overhead and arch slightly back.
3. Rest your back hand gently on your back thigh.
4. Keep your gaze upward or forward while maintaining a deep stretch.
5. Hold for a few breaths before switching sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your front knee stable and aligned with the ankle.
2. Engage your core to support your lower back.
3. Avoid collapsing into the back leg; keep the weight evenly distributed.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaUstrasana
string-array.item: Ustrasana
Ustrasana, or Camel Pose, is a deep backbend that stretches the front body while strengthening the back and shoulders.
This pose improves spinal flexibility, opens the chest, and helps counteract poor posture from prolonged sitting.
To perform the exercise:
1. Kneel on the floor with your knees hip-width apart.
2. Place your hands on your lower back for support.
3. Slowly lean back, reaching for your heels with your hands while keeping your hips forward.
4. Lift your chest and drop your head back gently, holding the pose for a few breaths.
5. To release, bring your hands back to your lower back and slowly return to an upright position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core to support your lower back.
2. Keep your thighs perpendicular to the floor to maintain proper alignment.
3. If reaching your heels is difficult, keep your hands on your lower back for support.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaUtthitaTrikonasana
string-array.item: Utthita Trikonasana (Extended Triangle Pose)
Utthita Trikonasana is a standing yoga pose that stretches the legs, hips, and spine while improving balance and stability.
This pose enhances flexibility in the hamstrings and strengthens the legs and core.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet wide apart, turning one foot outward at a 90-degree angle.
2. Extend your arms parallel to the floor.
3. Reach forward with your front hand and lower it to your shin, ankle, or the floor.
4. Extend your other arm toward the ceiling and turn your gaze upward.
5. Hold for a few breaths before switching sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your front knee slightly bent if you have tight hamstrings.
2. Engage your core to maintain stability.
3. Avoid collapsing into the lower side; instead, lift through the torso.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaTigerYogaPose
string-array.item: Tiger Yoga Pose
The Tiger Pose (Vyaghrasana) is a gentle backbend that strengthens the spine, core, and glutes while improving flexibility.
This pose also helps improve coordination and balance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a tabletop position on hands and knees.
2. Inhale and lift one leg backward, bending the knee.
3. If comfortable, reach back with the opposite hand to grasp the raised foot.
4. Hold the pose while keeping your balance and maintaining a steady breath.
5. Release and switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core for stability and control.
2. Keep your supporting arm strong and avoid collapsing into the shoulder.
3. If reaching the foot is difficult, practice lifting the leg first before attempting the full pose.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaBhekasanaFrogPose
string-array.item: Bhekasana (Frog Pose)
Bhekasana, or Frog Pose, is an intense quadriceps and hip flexor stretch that improves flexibility in the legs and opens the chest.
This pose enhances spinal mobility and is beneficial for improving posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on the mat with your legs extended.
2. Bend your knees and bring your feet toward your hips.
3. Reach back with your hands to grasp your feet, pressing them down toward the floor.
4. Lift your chest slightly and hold the pose for a few breaths.
5. Release slowly and return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your thighs grounded while pressing the feet down.
2. Engage your glutes to support the lower back.
3. If reaching both feet is challenging, practice with one leg at a time.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaBalasana
string-array.item: Balasana (Child\'s Pose)
Balasana, or Child’s Pose, is a resting pose that stretches the back, hips, and shoulders while promoting relaxation.
This pose helps relieve stress and tension while gently stretching the spine.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a kneeling position with your big toes touching and knees apart.
2. Lower your torso forward, extending your arms in front or alongside your body.
3. Rest your forehead on the mat and relax your shoulders.
4. Hold the pose for several breaths, focusing on deep breathing.
5. To release, slowly return to a seated position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your arms extended for an active stretch or rest them alongside your body for relaxation.
2. If your forehead doesn’t reach the floor, place a block or cushion for support.
3. Breathe deeply to enhance relaxation and release tension.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaAnuvittasana
string-array.item: Anuvittasana | Standing Backbend Pose
Anuvittasana, or Standing Backbend Pose, is a gentle backbend that opens the chest and strengthens the back while improving posture.
This pose enhances spinal flexibility and energizes the body.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
2. Place your hands on your lower back for support.
3. Inhale and lift your chest while gently arching your back.
4. Keep your gaze upward and hold the pose for a few breaths.
5. To release, slowly return to an upright position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core to protect your lower back.
2. Keep your knees slightly bent if you feel tension in your lower back.
3. Avoid straining the neck; keep movements smooth and controlled.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaAnjaneyasana
string-array.item: Anjaneyasana | Low Lunge Pose
Anjaneyasana, or Low Lunge Pose, is a deep hip-opening stretch that improves flexibility in the legs and strengthens the lower body.
This pose enhances balance and stability while relieving tension in the hips.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a lunge position with one foot forward and the other leg extended back.
2. Lower your back knee to the ground and rest the top of your foot on the floor.
3. Inhale and lift your arms overhead, reaching toward the sky.
4. Hold the pose for a few breaths, deepening the stretch.
5. To release, bring your hands down and switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your front knee aligned with your ankle to avoid strain.
2. Engage your core and lift your chest for better balance.
3. Use a cushion under the back knee for added comfort.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaEkaPadaSetuBandhaSarvangasana
string-array.item: Eka Pada Setu Bandha Sarvangasana
Eka Pada Setu Bandha Sarvangasana, or One-Legged Bridge Pose, is a variation of the Bridge Pose that strengthens the glutes, core, and hamstrings.
This pose enhances spinal flexibility while improving balance and coordination.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Press into your feet and lift your hips off the ground.
3. Extend one leg toward the ceiling while keeping your hips level.
4. Hold the position for a few breaths, then switch legs.
5. Lower your hips back down to release.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to maintain balance.
2. Avoid arching your lower back excessively.
3. Focus on controlled movements to maximize muscle engagement.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaDandayamanaBharmanasana
string-array.item: Dandayamana Bharmanasana | Balancing Table Pose
Dandayamana Bharmanasana, or Balancing Table Pose, is a yoga posture that strengthens the core, back, and shoulders while improving coordination.
This pose enhances stability and focus.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a tabletop position on hands and knees.
2. Extend your right arm forward and your left leg straight back.
3. Keep your hips level and engage your core for balance.
4. Hold the position for a few breaths, then switch sides.
5. Return to the starting position and repeat as needed.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your gaze focused on the floor to maintain balance.
2. Engage your glutes and core to keep your body stable.
3. Move slowly and with control to prevent wobbling.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaChaturangaDandasana
string-array.item: Chaturanga Dandasana | Low Plank Pose
Chaturanga Dandasana, or Low Plank Pose, is a foundational yoga pose that builds upper body strength and core stability.
This pose strengthens the arms, shoulders, chest, and abdominals.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a high plank position with your shoulders over your wrists.
2. Lower your body halfway down, keeping your elbows close to your ribs.
3. Maintain a straight line from head to heels.
4. Hold for a few breaths, then push back up or transition to another pose.
5. To release, lower your body completely to the mat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core to prevent sagging in the lower back.
2. Keep your elbows at a 90-degree angle to avoid straining your shoulders.
3. If needed, modify by lowering your knees for extra support.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaBitilasana
string-array.item: Bitilasana | Cow Pose
Bitilasana, or Cow Pose, is a simple yoga posture that warms up the spine, enhances flexibility, and relieves lower back tension.
This pose is often performed in combination with Cat Pose in a dynamic flow.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start on all fours, with wrists aligned under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Inhale and lift your head and chest, arching your back while tilting your tailbone upward.
3. Keep your shoulders relaxed and your breath steady.
4. Hold the position for a few seconds.
5. Exhale and transition into Cat Pose for a smooth movement.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep movements fluid and synchronized with your breath.
2. Avoid straining your neck by keeping it in a natural position.
3. Use a soft mat to support your knees for extra comfort.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaPadaHastasana
string-array.item: Pada Hastasana | Hands to Feet Pose
Pada Hastasana, or Hands to Feet Pose, is a deep forward bend that stretches the hamstrings, improves spinal flexibility, and boosts circulation.
This pose helps to relax the back muscles and reduce fatigue.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart.
2. Exhale as you slowly bend forward, reaching your hands toward the floor.
3. Relax your neck and let your head hang naturally.
4. Hold the position for several breaths.
5. Inhale and slowly return to the standing position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Slightly bend your knees if you feel too much tension.
2. Do not pull yourself down forcefully to avoid injury.
3. Breathe deeply, allowing your muscles to relax with each exhale.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaTitliAsana
string-array.item: Titli Asana | Butterfly Pose
Titli Asana, or Butterfly Pose, increases hip flexibility and stretches the inner thighs.
This pose helps release tension in the pelvic area and promotes relaxation.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the mat, bring the soles of your feet together, and pull them close to your pelvis.
2. Keep your spine straight and let your knees drop to the sides.
3. Begin gently bouncing your knees up and down like butterfly wings.
4. Continue the motion for a few breaths at a comfortable pace.
5. To release, straighten your legs in front of you.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Do not force your knees down; allow them to lower naturally.
2. Keep your back straight and avoid slouching.
3. If your hips are tight, place cushions under your thighs for support.

string-array.name: descriptionBaddhaKonasanaButterflyPose
string-array.item: Baddha Konasana | Butterfly Pose
A foundational seated yoga pose that opens the hips and stretches the inner thighs.
This pose improves flexibility in the groin and hip region while promoting relaxation.
To perform the pose:
1. Sit on the floor with legs extended straight
2. Bend knees and bring soles of feet together
3. Let knees fall outward, creating diamond shape with legs
4. Hold feet with hands and sit tall
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep spine long - avoid rounding back
2. Don\'t force knees down - let gravity work
3. Breathe deeply to enhance relaxation
4. Use props under knees if needed for support

string-array.name: descriptionYogaMakarasana
string-array.item: Makarasana | Crocodile Pose
Makarasana, or Crocodile Pose, is a relaxing yoga posture that relieves tension in the lower back and enhances deep breathing.
This pose is ideal for cooling down after an intense workout.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your stomach with legs extended and toes pointing slightly outward.
2. Place your arms in front of you, stacking your hands, and rest your forehead on them.
3. Close your eyes, relax completely, and breathe slowly.
4. Stay in this position for a few minutes, focusing on your breath.
5. To exit, gently roll onto your back or sit up.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your breathing slow and natural to maximize relaxation.
2. Ensure your body remains still to maintain a meditative state.
3. Use a cushion under your chest if you need extra support.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaArdhaUttanasana
string-array.item: Ardha Uttanasana | Standing Half Forward Bend
Ardha Uttanasana, or Standing Half Forward Bend, is a yoga posture that strengthens the back, stretches the hamstrings, and improves posture.
This pose is commonly performed as part of Sun Salutations and is beneficial for spinal alignment.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart and inhale while extending your arms overhead.
2. Exhale and hinge at your hips, lowering your torso halfway down while keeping your back straight.
3. Place your hands on your shins, thighs, or the floor, keeping your spine elongated.
4. Engage your core and hold the position for a few breaths.
5. Inhale and slowly return to a standing position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your shoulders.
2. Slightly bend your knees if your hamstrings feel too tight.
3. Engage your core for stability and balance.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaArdhaKapotasana
string-array.item: Ardha Kapotasana | Half Pigeon Pose
Ardha Kapotasana, or Half Pigeon Pose, is a deep hip-opening posture that stretches the hip flexors and lower back.
This pose is excellent for improving flexibility and releasing tension in the hips.
To perform the exercise:
1. Begin in a tabletop position with hands and knees on the mat.
2. Bring your right knee forward and place it behind your right wrist, extending your left leg back.
3. Keep your hips squared and slowly lower your upper body forward.
4. Rest your forehead on the mat and breathe deeply.
5. Hold the pose for 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your front foot flexed to protect your knee.
2. Place a yoga block under your hip for support if needed.
3. Breathe deeply to enhance relaxation and flexibility.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaAdvasana
string-array.item: Advasana | Reverse Corpse Pose
Advasana, or Reverse Corpse Pose, is a relaxation posture that calms the nervous system and releases tension from the body.
This pose is beneficial for deep relaxation and post-workout recovery.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face-down on the mat with legs extended and arms stretched forward.
2. Keep your forehead resting on the mat and relax your entire body.
3. Close your eyes and focus on deep, steady breathing.
4. Hold the position for a few minutes, allowing full relaxation.
5. To exit, gently roll onto your side before sitting up.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use a folded towel under your forehead for comfort.
2. Keep your breathing slow and steady to maximize relaxation.
3. Ensure your body remains completely still during the pose.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaAdhoMukhaVrksasana
string-array.item: Adho Mukha Vrksasana | Handstand Pose
Adho Mukha Vrksasana, or Handstand Pose, is an advanced inversion that strengthens the arms, shoulders, and core.
This pose improves balance, enhances focus, and builds upper-body endurance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a downward-facing dog position with hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Shift your weight forward and walk your feet closer to your hands.
3. Kick one leg up, followed by the other, to balance in a handstand.
4. Engage your core and keep your legs straight and together.
5. Hold the position as long as possible, then lower back down with control.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Practice against a wall for support when learning the pose.
2. Keep your fingers spread wide for better balance.
3. Engage your core and glutes to maintain stability.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaAdhoMukhaSvanasana
string-array.item: Adho Mukha Svanasana | Downward Facing Dog
Adho Mukha Svanasana, or Downward Facing Dog, is a fundamental yoga pose that strengthens the upper body and stretches the hamstrings, calves, and spine.
This pose enhances blood circulation and improves posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Start in a tabletop position with hands and knees on the mat.
2. Tuck your toes under and lift your hips toward the ceiling.
3. Straighten your legs while pressing your heels toward the ground.
4. Keep your head relaxed and arms extended, forming an inverted "V" shape.
5. Hold the pose for a few breaths, then release.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your hands and feet firmly grounded for stability.
2. Maintain a slight bend in the knees if needed.
3. Engage your core and avoid collapsing into your shoulders.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaTadasana
string-array.item: Tadasana | Mountain Pose
Tadasana, or Mountain Pose, is a foundational standing yoga posture that promotes good posture, balance, and alignment.
This pose helps improve body awareness, strengthen the legs, and enhance stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with feet together or hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Engage your thighs, lift your chest, and lengthen your spine.
3. Keep your shoulders relaxed and gaze forward.
4. Hold the position for several breaths, focusing on deep and steady breathing.
5. Release and return to a neutral standing posture.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Distribute your weight evenly across both feet.
2. Engage your core to support spinal alignment.
3. Keep your arms active but relaxed to avoid unnecessary tension.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaSuptaBaddhaKonasana
string-array.item: Supta Baddha Konasana | Reclining Bound Angle Pose
Supta Baddha Konasana, or Reclining Bound Angle Pose, is a restorative yoga posture that promotes relaxation, opens the hips, and enhances flexibility in the inner thighs.
This pose helps relieve stress, improve circulation, and gently stretch the groin and lower body.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the mat with your legs extended forward.
2. Bring the soles of your feet together, allowing your knees to fall open to the sides.
3. Slowly lower your upper body onto the mat, lying down with your arms relaxed at your sides.
4. Close your eyes, breathe deeply, and hold the position for 1 to 5 minutes.
5. To release, bring your knees together and sit up slowly.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use yoga blocks or pillows under your knees for extra support if needed.
2. Keep your breathing slow and steady to enhance relaxation.
3. Avoid forcing your knees to the ground; let gravity gently deepen the stretch.
4. Place a bolster or pillow under your back for additional support and a deeper chest opening.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaViparitaKarani
string-array.item: Viparita Karani | Legs Up the Wall Pose
Viparita Karani, or Legs Up the Wall Pose, is a restorative inversion that promotes relaxation, relieves leg fatigue, and improves circulation.
This pose is beneficial for reducing stress and swelling in the legs.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit next to a wall and lie back while swinging your legs up against the wall.
2. Adjust your hips close to the wall for a comfortable position.
3. Rest your arms at your sides with palms facing up.
4. Relax your body and breathe deeply, holding the pose for 5–10 minutes.
5. To release, bend your knees and roll to your side before sitting up.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Place a folded blanket under your lower back for extra support.
2. Maintain a relaxed neck and shoulders throughout the pose.
3. Focus on slow breathing to deepen relaxation and release tension.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaSuptaMatsyendrasana
string-array.item: Supta Matsyendrasana | Supine Spinal Twist
Supta Matsyendrasana, or Supine Spinal Twist, is a gentle twist that stretches the spine, massages the internal organs, and promotes relaxation.
This pose helps release tension in the back and improves spinal flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your legs extended.
2. Bend your right knee and bring it across your body to the left side.
3. Extend your right arm out to the side and turn your head to the right.
4. Keep both shoulders grounded and breathe deeply.
5. Hold the pose for 30 seconds to 1 minute, then switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your shoulders pressed against the mat for a deeper twist.
2. Use a cushion under your bent knee if needed for support.
3. Breathe deeply to enhance spinal release and relaxation.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaSamakonasana
string-array.item: Samakonasana | Straight Angle Pose
Samakonasana, or Straight Angle Pose, is an advanced flexibility pose that deeply stretches the hamstrings, inner thighs, and lower back.
This pose helps improve flexibility and strengthens the legs.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight to the sides.
2. Keep your toes pointing upward and your knees straight.
3. Slowly lean forward from your hips, keeping your back straight.
4. Rest your hands on the floor or reach forward as far as possible.
5. Hold the pose for 30 seconds to 1 minute, then release.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your spine.
2. Move into the stretch gradually to prevent injury.
3. If necessary, use yoga blocks for support under your hands.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaShoulderstand
string-array.item: Shoulderstand | Salamba Sarvangasana
Salamba Sarvangasana, or Shoulderstand, is an advanced inversion pose that strengthens the shoulders, improves circulation, and enhances core stability.
This pose helps stimulate the thyroid gland, improve posture, and calm the nervous system.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your arms at your sides.
2. Lift your legs towards the ceiling, using your hands to support your lower back.
3. Engage your core and straighten your legs while keeping your neck relaxed.
4. Hold the position for 30 seconds to 1 minute, breathing deeply.
5. Slowly lower your legs back to the mat with control.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your elbows close to your body for better support.
2. Avoid putting excessive pressure on your neck.
3. Use a folded blanket under your shoulders for comfort.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaNaukaSanchalanasan
string-array.item: Nauka Sanchalanasan | Rowing the Boat Pose
Nauka Sanchalanasan, or Rowing the Boat Pose, is a dynamic yoga posture that strengthens the core, improves spinal flexibility, and enhances balance.
This pose mimics the movement of rowing a boat, engaging the abdominal muscles and improving coordination.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the mat with your legs extended forward.
2. Clasp your hands together as if holding an oar.
3. Lean back slightly and move your hands in a circular motion as if rowing a boat.
4. Keep your core engaged and maintain a steady breath.
5. Repeat for 10-15 rounds, then relax.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight to avoid strain.
2. Engage your core throughout the movement.
3. Perform the exercise slowly and with control.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaMalasana
string-array.item: Malasana | Squat Pose or Garland Pose
Malasana, or Squat Pose, is a deep hip-opening yoga posture that improves mobility, strengthens the lower body, and enhances digestion.
This pose is beneficial for increasing flexibility in the hips and ankles while promoting grounding and relaxation.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand with your feet slightly wider than hip-width apart.
2. Lower your hips into a deep squat, bringing your palms together in front of your chest.
3. Keep your back straight and chest lifted.
4. Hold the pose for 30 seconds to 1 minute, breathing deeply.
5. To release, press through your heels and stand back up.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use a yoga block under your hips for support if needed.
2. Keep your feet flat on the ground and avoid lifting your heels.
3. Engage your core for balance and stability.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaFullLotusPose
string-array.item: Full Lotus Pose
Full Lotus Pose is a traditional seated meditation posture that enhances flexibility in the hips, knees, and ankles.
This pose promotes mindfulness, relaxation, and improved posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the mat with your legs extended forward.
2. Bend your right knee and place your foot on top of your left thigh.
3. Bend your left knee and place your foot on top of your right thigh.
4. Keep your spine straight and hands resting on your knees.
5. Hold the pose for 1-5 minutes, breathing deeply.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and shoulders relaxed.
2. Avoid forcing your knees down; let them rest naturally.
3. Use a cushion or blanket under your hips for comfort.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaHalasana
string-array.item: Halasana | Plow Pose
Halasana, or Plow Pose, is an advanced yoga posture that stretches the spine, shoulders, and hamstrings while calming the nervous system.
This pose helps improve flexibility, relieve stress, and stimulate the digestive organs.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your arms at your sides.
2. Lift your legs over your head, reaching your toes towards the floor behind you.
3. Keep your hands on your lower back for support or extend them on the mat.
4. Hold the position for 30 seconds to 1 minute, breathing deeply.
5. Slowly roll your spine back down to the mat with control.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your neck relaxed and avoid excessive pressure on your spine.
2. Engage your core muscles for better control.
3. Use a folded blanket under your shoulders for support.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaLocustPose
string-array.item: Locust Pose
Locust Pose is a back-strengthening yoga posture that targets the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings while improving spinal flexibility.
This pose enhances posture, strengthens the core, and helps alleviate lower back pain.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on the mat with your arms at your sides and palms facing down.
2. Inhale and lift your chest, arms, and legs off the ground simultaneously.
3. Engage your core and squeeze your glutes, keeping your gaze forward.
4. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds, breathing steadily.
5. Exhale and slowly lower back down to the mat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your legs straight and avoid bending the knees.
2. Engage your lower back and core for stability.
3. Do not overextend your neck; keep it in a neutral position.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaWheelPose
string-array.item: Wheel Pose | Chakrasana | Urdhva Dhanurasana
Wheel Pose, or Chakrasana, is an advanced backbend that strengthens the entire body, improves flexibility, and energizes the nervous system.
This pose opens the chest, shoulders, and hips, enhancing overall spinal mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet hip-width apart.
2. Place your hands beside your head, fingers pointing toward your shoulders.
3. Press into your hands and feet, lifting your hips and chest off the mat.
4. Straighten your arms and legs, arching your back and opening your heart.
5. Hold the pose for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply.
6. Slowly lower yourself back down with control.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Warm up your back and shoulders before attempting this pose.
2. Engage your core and glutes for better stability.
3. If necessary, use a yoga block under your hands or feet for support.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaGarudasana
string-array.item: Garudasana | Eagle Pose
Garudasana, or Eagle Pose, is a balancing yoga posture that strengthens the legs, improves focus, and enhances flexibility in the shoulders and hips.
This pose promotes concentration, coordination, and deep muscle engagement.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand tall with your feet together and arms at your sides.
2. Bend your knees slightly and lift your right leg over your left thigh, wrapping it around your left calf.
3. Cross your right arm under your left arm, bringing your palms together.
4. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds, maintaining steady breaths.
5. Release and repeat on the opposite side.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Focus on a fixed point to maintain balance.
2. Engage your core to stabilize your posture.
3. If you struggle with balance, use a wall for support or perform the pose with the lifted foot resting on the ground.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaCrabPose
string-array.item: Crab Pose
Crab Pose is a yoga posture that strengthens the arms, shoulders, and core while improving flexibility in the spine and hip flexors.
This pose enhances coordination and body awareness while promoting shoulder stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the mat with your feet flat and hands placed behind you, fingers pointing forward.
2. Press into your hands and feet to lift your hips off the ground.
3. Engage your core and keep your chest open.
4. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds while breathing steadily.
5. Slowly lower your hips back down to the mat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your wrists aligned under your shoulders for support.
2. Engage your glutes and core to maintain stability.
3. If you feel wrist discomfort, adjust your hand placement or use a yoga block for support.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaChildsPoseToCobra
string-array.item: Child’s Pose to Cobra Pose
This dynamic yoga sequence transitions between Child’s Pose and Cobra Pose, stretching the spine, opening the chest, and promoting relaxation.
The movement between these two poses helps improve flexibility and reduce tension in the back and shoulders.
To perform the exercise:
1. Begin in Child’s Pose, sitting on your heels with your arms extended forward.
2. Inhale and shift forward into Cobra Pose, lifting your chest while keeping your legs and pelvis grounded.
3. Hold the Cobra Pose for a breath, then exhale and return to Child’s Pose.
4. Repeat the transition 5-10 times, moving with your breath.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your movements slow and controlled.
2. Engage your core when transitioning between poses.
3. If Cobra Pose feels too intense, modify by keeping your elbows bent and chest lower to the ground.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaCamelPose
string-array.item: Camel Pose
Camel Pose, or Ustrasana, is a deep backbend that stretches the front of the body while strengthening the back muscles.
This pose improves spinal flexibility, opens the chest, and enhances posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Kneel on the mat with your knees hip-width apart and hands resting on your lower back.
2. Slowly arch your back, reaching your hands towards your heels.
3. Keep your chest lifted and engage your core for support.
4. Hold the pose for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply.
5. Slowly return to the starting position by engaging your core and lifting your torso upright.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your thighs perpendicular to the ground.
2. Avoid straining your lower back; focus on opening your chest.
3. If reaching your heels is difficult, place your hands on your lower back for support.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaBridgePose
string-array.item: Bridge Pose
Bridge Pose, or Setu Bandhasana, is a backbend that strengthens the spine, glutes, and hamstrings while opening the chest and shoulders.
This pose helps relieve lower back pain and promotes relaxation.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet hip-width apart.
2. Press into your feet and lift your hips towards the ceiling.
3. Keep your arms alongside your body or clasp your hands underneath your back.
4. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds while breathing deeply.
5. Slowly lower your hips back to the mat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your glutes and core for stability.
2. Avoid arching your lower back too much; focus on lifting through the hips.
3. If needed, place a yoga block under your sacrum for support.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaSaithalyasana
string-array.item: Saithalyasana | Animal Relaxation Pose
Saithalyasana, or Animal Relaxation Pose, is a seated forward bend that promotes deep relaxation and releases tension in the spine and hips.
This pose is often used for stress relief and calming the nervous system.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the mat with your legs folded under you in a comfortable position.
2. Slowly bend forward, extending your arms in front of you.
3. Rest your forehead on the mat and allow your body to relax completely.
4. Hold the position for 30-60 seconds, breathing deeply.
5. Slowly rise back up to a seated position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your hips grounded while reaching forward.
2. Focus on deep, slow breaths to enhance relaxation.
3. If needed, place a cushion under your forehead for extra comfort.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaUpavisthaKonasana
string-array.item: Upavistha Konasana | Seated Wide-Legged Forward Bend
Upavistha Konasana is a deep forward bend that stretches the inner thighs, hamstrings, and lower back.
This pose improves flexibility in the legs and promotes relaxation.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the mat with your legs extended wide apart.
2. Keep your spine straight and slowly lean forward, reaching your hands towards your feet.
3. Engage your core and avoid rounding your lower back.
4. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds while breathing deeply.
5. Slowly return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your knees slightly bent if your hamstrings feel too tight.
2. Focus on lengthening your spine as you fold forward.
3. Use yoga blocks under your hands for support if needed.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaBhujangasana
string-array.item: Bhujangasana | Cobra Abdominal Stretch
Bhujangasana, or Cobra Pose, is a backbend that strengthens the spine and opens the chest, improving posture and flexibility.
This pose energizes the body and helps relieve back stiffness.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your stomach with your hands placed under your shoulders.
2. Inhale and lift your chest, straightening your arms while keeping your legs and pelvis grounded.
3. Engage your core and keep your shoulders relaxed.
4. Hold the pose for 20-30 seconds while breathing deeply.
5. Exhale and slowly lower back to the mat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your elbows slightly bent if you feel tension in your lower back.
2. Engage your glutes and core for better support.
3. Avoid overextending your neck; keep your gaze forward or slightly upward.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaFishPose
string-array.item: Fish Pose
Fish Pose, or Matsyasana, is a chest-opening yoga pose that stretches the throat, chest, and shoulders while strengthening the upper back.
This pose improves posture, relieves tension in the neck and shoulders, and enhances lung capacity.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your legs extended and arms resting beside your body.
2. Place your hands under your glutes and press your forearms into the ground.
3. Inhale and lift your chest while tilting your head back so the crown of your head rests lightly on the mat.
4. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply.
5. Exhale and slowly lower your chest and head back to the mat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core and press your forearms into the floor for support.
2. Avoid putting too much pressure on your head; the weight should be supported by your arms.
3. If needed, modify by placing a yoga block under your upper back for a gentler stretch.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaBowPose
string-array.item: Bow Pose
Bow Pose, or Dhanurasana, is a deep backbend that stretches the front of the body while strengthening the back muscles.
This pose improves spinal flexibility, stimulates digestion, and opens the chest and shoulders.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your stomach with your arms alongside your body and legs extended.
2. Bend your knees and reach back to grab your ankles.
3. Inhale and lift your chest and legs off the mat, pulling your feet upwards.
4. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds while breathing deeply.
5. Exhale and slowly lower back to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your thighs hip-width apart to maintain balance.
2. Engage your core and avoid straining your lower back.
3. If it\'s difficult to reach your ankles, use a yoga strap around your feet for assistance.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaCatCowPose
string-array.item: Cat-Cow Pose
Cat-Cow Pose, or Marjaryasana-Bitilasana, is a gentle yoga flow that enhances spinal flexibility and relieves tension in the back.
This pose improves posture, stretches the neck and shoulders, and promotes relaxation.
To perform the exercise:
1. Begin on all fours with your wrists under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
2. Inhale, arch your back, lift your tailbone, and look up (Cow Pose).
3. Exhale, round your spine, tuck your chin to your chest, and draw your belly inward (Cat Pose).
4. Continue flowing between these two positions for 5-10 breaths.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Move slowly and with control, syncing movement with breath.
2. Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid hunching them.
3. Modify by placing a cushion under your knees for extra comfort.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaAbdominalBracing
string-array.item: Abdominal Bracing
Abdominal Bracing is a core-strengthening exercise that improves stability, supports the lower back, and enhances posture.
This technique is used in many workouts to engage the deep core muscles.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Tighten your core as if bracing for impact without holding your breath.
3. Hold the contraction for 10-20 seconds while maintaining steady breathing.
4. Release and repeat for several repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your spine in a neutral position without arching or flattening your lower back.
2. Engage your deep abdominal muscles without tensing your neck or shoulders.
3. Gradually increase the duration as your core strength improves.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaDoublePigeonPose
string-array.item: Double Pigeon Pose
Double Pigeon Pose, or Agnistambhasana, is a deep hip opener that stretches the glutes, outer thighs, and lower back.
This pose helps release tension in the hips and improves flexibility in the lower body.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the mat with your legs extended in front of you.
2. Bend one knee and stack your shin parallel to the front edge of the mat.
3. Place the other shin on top, aligning the knees and ankles.
4. Lean forward slightly to deepen the stretch, keeping your spine long.
5. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your feet flexed to protect your knees.
2. If your top knee is elevated, place a cushion under it for support.
3. Move slowly and listen to your body to avoid overstretching.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaFrogPose
string-array.item: Frog Pose
Frog Pose, or Bhekasana, is a deep hip-opening yoga pose that stretches the inner thighs, groin, and hips while improving flexibility.
This pose enhances mobility in the hips, relieves tension in the lower back, and is beneficial for those with tight hip flexors.
To perform the exercise:
1. Begin on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
2. Slowly widen your knees as far as comfortable, keeping your ankles in line with your knees.
3. Lower your forearms to the mat and press your hips back slightly.
4. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds while breathing deeply.
5. To release, bring your knees back together and return to a seated or kneeling position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your core engaged to support your lower back.
2. If the stretch is too intense, place a cushion under your knees for support.
3. Move slowly and avoid forcing your knees too wide to prevent strain.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaSupineSpinalTwist
string-array.item: Supine Spinal Twist
Supine Spinal Twist, or Supta Matsyendrasana, is a restorative yoga pose that stretches the spine, lower back, and obliques.
This pose helps release tension in the back, improves spinal mobility, and promotes relaxation.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your legs extended.
2. Bend one knee and bring it across your body toward the opposite side.
3. Extend your opposite arm and look in the opposite direction.
4. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds while breathing deeply.
5. Return to the center and repeat on the other side.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep both shoulders grounded on the mat for a deeper stretch.
2. Modify by placing a pillow under your bent knee if needed.
3. Relax into the twist and avoid forcing the movement.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaParsvaBalasana
string-array.item: Parsva Balasana | Thread the Needle Pose
Parsva Balasana, or Thread the Needle Pose, is a gentle twisting yoga posture that stretches the shoulders, upper back, and neck while promoting spinal mobility and relaxation.
This pose helps relieve tension in the upper body, improves flexibility, and encourages deep breathing.
To perform the exercise:
1. Begin in a tabletop position with your hands and knees on the mat.
2. Inhale and lift your right arm toward the ceiling, opening your chest.
3. Exhale and thread your right arm under your left arm, bringing your right shoulder and cheek to rest on the mat.
4. Keep your hips aligned and extend your left arm forward or rest it on your lower back.
5. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply.
6. Inhale to lift your right arm back up and return to the starting position.
7. Repeat on the other side.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your hips square and avoid shifting them to one side.
2. Maintain a gentle stretch without forcing the twist.
3. Relax your neck and allow your upper body to sink into the stretch.
4. Use a yoga block under your shoulder if you need additional support.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaHalfFrogPose
string-array.item: Half Frog Pose
Half Frog Pose, or Ardha Bhekasana, is a backbend and quad-stretching yoga pose that increases flexibility in the hip flexors and thighs.
This pose strengthens the spine, improves posture, and relieves tightness in the front body.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your stomach with your legs extended.
2. Bend one knee and reach back to grab your ankle with the same-side hand.
3. Press your foot toward your glute while lifting your chest.
4. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds while breathing deeply.
5. Release and switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your hips pressed into the mat to maintain stability.
2. Use a yoga strap around your foot if you have limited flexibility.
3. Avoid excessive arching in your lower back by engaging your core.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaHappyBabyPose
string-array.item: Happy Baby Pose
Happy Baby Pose, or Ananda Balasana, is a relaxing yoga pose that stretches the hips, inner thighs, and lower back.
This pose helps reduce stress, release lower back tension, and improve hip flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back and bring your knees toward your chest.
2. Grab the outer edges of your feet with your hands.
3. Open your knees wider than your torso and gently rock side to side.
4. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds while breathing deeply.
5. Release and return to a neutral position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your lower back pressed into the mat to prevent strain.
2. Modify by holding your shins if reaching your feet is difficult.
3. Relax your shoulders and let gravity help deepen the stretch.

string-array.name: descriptionYogaDhanurasana
string-array.item: Dhanurasana | Rocking Bow Pose

Dhanurasana, or Rocking Bow Pose, is a powerful backbend that stretches the entire front body while strengthening the back muscles. It improves flexibility in the spine and opens the chest and shoulders.
This pose enhances posture, stimulates the digestive organs, and increases spinal mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your stomach with your arms resting by your sides.
2. Bend your knees and bring your heels toward your glutes.
3. Reach back and grasp your ankles with both hands.
4. Inhale and lift your chest, pulling your legs upward to form a bow shape.
5. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds while maintaining steady breathing.
6. For the rocking variation, gently rock forward and backward by shifting your weight.
7. Exhale and slowly release the pose, lowering your legs and chest to the mat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Engage your core and legs to avoid excessive lower back compression.
2. Keep your neck relaxed and gaze slightly forward.
3. If reaching your ankles is difficult, use a yoga strap around your feet.
4. Perform the rocking motion smoothly and avoid abrupt movements.
